馬克樹是一種金屬打擊樂器，音色明亮刺激而富有穿透力，具有獨特的金屬質感。其高頻泛: The mark tree is a metal percussion instrument with a bright, exciting and strongly penetrating timbre and a distinct metallic quality. Its high overtones are rich, and it can produce a crisp, glittering sound. Its range lies in the treble, and a stroke produces a series of bright points of sound that decay quickly. The mark tree resonates through the collision of the metal tubes, each of which can vibrate on its own, so its sound has layered frequency components. Compared with the warm depth of the glockenspiel, the mark tree is sharper and more pointed; compared with the triangle, it is louder, with more complex and richer overtones. The instrument is often used to heighten tense dramatic scenes or to create a thoroughly modern atmosphere.

The mark tree is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.232, designed in 1967 by the studio percussionist Mark Stevens and also called the nail tree, bell tree or bar chimes. It consists of a number of solid aluminium or brass tubes of different lengths, about three-eighths of an inch in diameter, hung from a crossbar, usually in order of pitch; the fingers or a stick are swept across the tubes to produce a rising or falling glissando, and the more expensive models have a damper bar. It has no definite pitch, unlike tubular bells, and it differs from wind chimes in construction and in the way it sounds; it is used mainly to add colour to the music, and appears in modern repertoire.
